lit.\u0027¿Cuál es el único planeta menos de: "Which is the only planet less dense than water?"

lit.\u0027¿Qué planeta gira «acostado», con: "Which planet rotates “lying down”, with its axis tilted about 98°?"

lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e\u003cb\u003e1.ª ley::
"

1st law: orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus (Mercury's is the most eccentric of the planets).

2nd law: the radius vector sweeps equal areas in equal times: the two sectors (yellow and sky blue) cover the same time and have the same area, although they have different shapes. Near perihelion the planet moves faster.

3rd law: T² ∝ a³ (Kepler tab).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eSol\u:
"

The Sun contains 99.86 % of the mass of the Solar System. In its core (≈ 15 million °C) hydrogen fuses into helium and releases the energy that reaches all the planets.

Its gravity keeps every body in orbit.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEntre Marte y Júpiter:
"

Between Mars and Jupiter, millions of rocky bodies orbit (2.1–3.3 AU), remnants of the formation of the system that Jupiter's gravity prevented from gathering into a planet.

Their total mass is only ≈ 3 % of that of the Moon. The largest, Ceres, is a dwarf planet.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eJúpiter y Saturno son:
"

Jupiter and Saturn are enormous and are made mostly of hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface. Jupiter equals 318 Earths.

Saturn has ice rings and a density lower than that of water. Both have dozens of satellites; look for the Galilean moons and Titan.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos planetas interior:
"

The inner planets are small and dense, with a solid surface and a metallic core. They have few satellites or none.

They are close to the Sun, so their years are short: Mercury takes 88 days; Mars, 687.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eMás allá de Neptuno h:
"

Beyond Neptune there is a belt of icy bodies (30–50 AU). Pluto, a dwarf planet since 2006, has a very eccentric orbit (e = 0.25) inclined 17° with respect to the plane of the planets.

Watch how its orbit leaves the plane.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eSol\u:
"

One Sun, 8 planets and billions of minor bodies. The distances here are compressed: in reality sunlight takes 8 min 20 s to reach Earth and about 4 h 10 min to reach Neptune.

Choose a body to see its fact sheet, or switch to “To scale” to see the real sizes relative to the Sun.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUrano y Neptuno tiene:
"

Uranus and Neptune have a mantle of water, ammonia and methane beneath an atmosphere of hydrogen and helium. Methane gives them their blue color.

Uranus rotates “lying down” (axis at 98°) and Neptune has the fastest winds. Their years last 84 and 165 Earth years.

"
lit.\u0027≈ 3 % de la masa de la Luna\u0027: "≈ 3 % of the mass of the Moon"
lit.\u0027≈ 73 % de hidrógeno y ≈ 25 % de he: "≈ 73 % hydrogen and ≈ 25 % helium (by mass), with traces of oxygen, carbon, neon and iron. In the core, hydrogen fuses into helium and releases energy."
lit.\u0027≈ 78 % N₂, ≈ 21 % O₂ y ≈ 0,9 % arg: "≈ 78 % N₂, ≈ 21 % O₂ and ≈ 0.9 % argon, with variable water vapor and CO₂. The ozone layer filters a large part of the ultraviolet radiation."
lit.\u0027≈ 90 % H₂ y ≈ 10 % He, con amoníac: "≈ 90 % H₂ and ≈ 10 % He, with ammonia, methane and water vapor. It has no solid surface: beneath the clouds, the pressure turns hydrogen into a liquid and then into a metal."
lit.\u0027≈ 95 % N₂ y ≈ 5 % CH₄, con una pre: "≈ 95 % N₂ and ≈ 5 % CH₄, with a surface pressure ≈ 1.5 times Earth's."
lit.\u0027≈ 96 % H₂ y ≈ 3 % He, con metano y: "≈ 96 % H₂ and ≈ 3 % He, with methane and ammonia. Its mean density (0.69 g/cm³) is lower than that of water: it would “float” in a large enough ocean."
lit.\u0027≈ 96,5 % de CO₂ y ≈ 3,5 % de N₂, c: "≈ 96.5 % CO₂ and ≈ 3.5 % N₂, with sulfuric acid clouds. The surface pressure is about 92 times Earth's. The greenhouse effect makes it hotter than Mercury."
lit.\u0027Atmósfera tenue de N₂, CH₄ y CO qu: "Thin atmosphere of N₂, CH₄ and CO that freezes and falls onto the surface as it moves away from the Sun. Its surface has nitrogen, methane and CO ices; the light heart-shaped region is called Tombaugh Regio."
lit.\u0027Azufre y compuestos de azufre (ama: "Sulfur and sulfur compounds (yellow, red and white) and a very thin atmosphere of SO₂."
lit.\u0027C (carbonosos, los más comunes), S: "C (carbonaceous, the most common), S (silicates) and M (metallic)."
lit.\u0027Cada segundo convierte unos 4 mill: "Every second it converts about 4 million tonnes of matter into energy. Its light takes 8 min 20 s to reach Earth, but the energy generated in the core takes tens of thousands of years to get out."
lit.\u0027Casi inexistente: solo una exosfer: "Almost nonexistent: just a tenuous exosphere of sodium, oxygen, hydrogen and helium. With no atmosphere to distribute heat, the day is scorching and the night, freezing."
lit.\u0027Casi un gemelo de la Tierra en tam: "Almost a twin of Earth in size and mass, but with a hellish environment. It rotates in the opposite direction to most planets (retrograde rotation) and its sidereal day lasts longer than its year."
lit.\u0027Cerca del Sol el radio vector es c: "Near the Sun the radius vector is short, so the planet must cover more arc in the same time."
lit.\u0027Con una atmósfera tan densa y una: "With such a dense atmosphere and such low gravity, in theory a person could fly by flapping wings tied to the arms."
lit.\u0027Corteza de hielo de agua sobre un: "Crust of water ice over a global ocean of salty liquid water, with more water than all of Earth's oceans."
lit.\u0027Dawn visitó Vesta y Ceres; OSIRIS-: "Dawn visited Vesta and Ceres; OSIRIS-REx brought samples from Bennu (2023); Hayabusa2 brought samples from Ryugu; the DART mission deflected the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022."
lit.\u0027Desde su descubrimiento en 1846 co: "Since its discovery in 1846 it has completed only one orbit around the Sun, in 2011."
lit.\u0027El «planeta rojo»: su color viene: "The “red planet”: its color comes from the iron oxide in the dust. It has the tallest volcano in the Solar System (Olympus Mons, ≈ 22 km), a canyon about 4,000 km long (Valles Marineris) and polar caps of water ice and CO₂."
lit.\u0027El centro de masa del par queda fu: "The center of mass of the pair lies outside Pluto, which is why it is considered a double system."
lit.\u0027El cinturón de asteroides se ubica: "The asteroid belt is located between the orbits of…"
lit.\u0027El de los anillos, menos denso que: "The one with rings, less dense than water."
lit.\u0027El gigante gaseoso: tiene más del: "The gas giant: it has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined. Its extremely fast rotation flattens it and arranges its clouds in bands. The Great Red Spot is an anticyclonic storm wider than Earth, observed for more than 150 years."
lit.\u0027El más cercano al Sol y el más peq: "The closest to the Sun and the smallest."
lit.\u0027El más lejano; tiene los vientos m: "The farthest; it has the fastest winds."
lit.\u0027El planeta más pequeño y el más ce: "The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. Its cratered surface resembles that of the Moon. It has an enormous iron core, occupying about 85 % of its radius."
lit.\u0027El planeta rojo, con el volcán más: "The red planet, with the tallest known volcano."
lit.\u0027El Sol: la estrella que lo gobiern: "The Sun: the star that governs it all"
"The only known place with life. It is the largest and densest rocky planet in the Solar System, with ≈ 71 % of its surface covered by liquid water and a magnetic field that deflects the solar wind."
lit.\u0027El único planeta con vida conocida: "The only planet with known life and liquid water on its surface."
lit.\u0027En Júpiter g = 24,8 m/s², el valor: "On Jupiter g = 24.8 m/s², the highest value of the planets (weight ≈ 1,490 N, versus 589 N on Earth)."
lit.\u0027En su polo norte hay una tormenta: "At its north pole there is a hexagonal storm about 30,000 km wide. The rings may be relatively young (hundreds of millions of years)."
lit.\u0027Entre 2,1 y 3,3 UA, entre Marte y: "Between 2.1 and 3.3 AU, between Mars and Jupiter."
lit.\u0027es demasiado pequeño para ser esfé: "it is too small to be spherical"
lit.\u0027Es el astro más brillante del ciel: "It is the brightest object in the sky after the Moon and is called the “morning star” or “evening star”. A sidereal day (243 d) lasts longer than a year (225 d)."
lit.\u0027Es el planeta más explorado despué: "It is the most explored planet after Earth: Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance (which looks for signs of ancient life in Jezero crater), with the Ingenuity helicopter."
lit.\u0027Es el planeta mejor estudiado: sat: "It is the best-studied planet: observation satellites (Landsat, Sentinel), the International Space Station and sensor networks on land, sea and air."
lit.\u0027Es la estrella en el centro; conti: "It is the star at the center; it contains 99.86 % of the mass."
lit.\u0027Es unas 20 veces más ancho y entre: "It is about 20 times wider and between 20 and 200 times more massive than the asteroid belt."
lit.\u0027Es uno de los lugares más prometed: "It is one of the most promising places to look for life beyond Earth."
lit.\u0027Estrella enana amarilla de tipo es: "Yellow dwarf star of spectral type G2V. It holds 99.86 % of the mass of the Solar System, so its gravity governs the motion of all the other bodies."
lit.\u0027Europa Clipper (NASA, lanzada en 2: "Europa Clipper (NASA, launched in 2024) will fly by it dozens of times; the JUICE mission (ESA) will study the system."
lit.\u0027Famoso por sus anillos, formados p: "Famous for its rings, formed by particles of water ice and rock ranging from dust grains to blocks the size of houses. The main rings extend about 280,000 km, but their typical thickness is only about 10 meters."
lit.\u0027Galileo descubrió Ío en 1610 junto: "Galileo discovered Io in 1610 together with the other three “Galilean” moons: they showed that not everything revolves around Earth."
lit.\u0027Galileo y Juno la sobrevolaron; JU: "Galileo and Juno flew by it; JUICE (ESA) will orbit it around 2031."
lit.\u0027Gigante helado que «rueda» de lado: "Ice giant that “rolls” on its side: its axis is tilted ≈ 98°, probably because of an ancient collision, so each pole receives continuous sunlight for about 42 years. It has 13 narrow, dark rings."
lit.\u0027Gigante helado y el planeta más le: "Ice giant and the planet farthest from the Sun. Its existence was predicted by calculation (Le Verrier and Adams) from the perturbations of Uranus and confirmed by observation in 1846 (Galle). It has the fastest winds in the Solar System, up to ≈ 2,100 km/h."
lit.\u0027Gira «acostado»: su eje está incli: "It rotates “lying down”: its axis is tilted almost 98°."
lit.\u0027H₂ (≈ 83 %), He (≈ 15 %) y metano: "H₂ (≈ 83 %), He (≈ 15 %) and methane (≈ 2 %); methane absorbs red and gives it its blue-green color. Beneath the atmosphere there is a dense mantle of water, ammonia and methane."
lit.\u0027H₂, He y ≈ 1,5 % de metano; su azu: "H₂, He and ≈ 1.5 % methane; its intense blue is due to methane and to other substances still under study."
lit.\u0027Hay evidencia de que hace miles de: "There is evidence that billions of years ago it had rivers and lakes of liquid water. A Martian day lasts about 40 minutes longer than an Earth one."
lit.\u0027Hielo de agua y roca; su polo nort: "Water ice and rock; its reddish north pole (Mordor Macula) is due to organic compounds called tholins."
lit.\u0027Hielo mezclado con roca y material: "Ice mixed with rock and dark material."
lit.\u0027Hielos de agua, metano y amoníaco: "Ices of water, methane and ammonia with rock"
lit.\u0027Hielos de nitrógeno, entre los lug: "Nitrogen ices, among the coldest places in the Solar System, with nitrogen geysers observed by Voyager 2."
lit.\u0027Irradia más calor del que recibe d: "It radiates more heat than it receives from the Sun: it is still releasing energy from its formation. It has the strongest magnetic field of the planets."
lit.\u0027Júpiter tiene un diámetro de ≈ 140: "Jupiter has a diameter of ≈ 140,000 km and a mass 318 times that of Earth."
lit.\u0027La densidad media de Saturno es 0,: "Saturn's mean density is 0.69 g/cm³ (that of water is 1 g/cm³)."
lit.\u0027La luna con atmósfera densa y lago: "The moon with a dense atmosphere and methane lakes."
lit.\u0027La luna galileana más cercana a Jú: "The Galilean moon closest to Jupiter and the body with the most volcanic activity in the Solar System, with hundreds of volcanoes. Its heat comes from the tides that Jupiter causes and from its resonance with Europa and Ganymede."
lit.\u0027La luna más grande del Sistema Sol: "The largest moon in the Solar System."
"The largest moon in the Solar System: larger than Mercury, although with less mass. It is the only known satellite with its own magnetic field."
lit.\u0027La luna más volcánica del Sistema: "The most volcanic moon in the Solar System."
lit.\u0027La mayor luna de Neptuno. Orbita e: "Neptune's largest moon. It orbits in the direction opposite to the planet's rotation (retrograde orbit), which suggests it is a Kuiper belt object captured by Neptune."
lit.\u0027La mayor luna de Plutón, con la mi: "Pluto's largest moon, with half its diameter. Pluto and Charon are in synchronous rotation: they always show each other the same face."
lit.\u0027La mayor luna de Plutón; forman un: "Pluto's largest moon; they form a double system."
lit.\u0027La mayor luna de Saturno y la únic: "Saturn's largest moon and the only one with a dense atmosphere. It has rivers, lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane."
lit.\u0027La segunda ley de Kepler (áreas ig: "Kepler's second law (equal areas in equal times) implies that a planet moves…"
lit.\u0027La sonda Huygens (ESA) aterrizó en: "The Huygens probe (ESA) landed in 2005. Dragonfly (NASA), a drone with rotors, will arrive around 2034."
lit.\u0027La UAI exige a un planeta haber de: "The IAU requires a planet to have cleared the neighborhood of its orbit; Pluto shares its own with the Kuiper belt."
lit.\u0027Las estaciones se deben a la incli: "The seasons are due to the tilt of the axis (23.4°) and not to the distance from the Sun: Earth passes closer to the Sun (perihelion) in January than in July."
lit.\u0027Los huecos de Kirkwood, causados p: "The Kirkwood gaps, caused by resonances with Jupiter, have almost no asteroids."
lit.\u0027Mariner 10 (1974–75), MESSENGER (e: "Mariner 10 (1974–75), MESSENGER (in orbit 2011–2015) and BepiColombo (ESA/JAXA), which reaches its orbit toward the end of 2026."
lit.\u0027Más allá aún está la nube de Oort,: "Even farther out is the Oort cloud, a hypothetical spherical region of comets reaching tens of thousands of AU."
lit.\u0027Mezcla de hielo y roca; probableme: "Mixture of ice and rock; it probably has a subsurface salty ocean."
lit.\u0027Miles; se estiman cientos de miles: "Thousands; hundreds of thousands of more than 100 km are estimated"
lit.\u0027Millones de cuerpos rocosos y metá: "Millions of rocky and metallic bodies, remnants of the formation of the Solar System that did not manage to form a planet, partly because of Jupiter's gravity. Despite what many films show, they are very far apart from one another."
lit.\u0027Millones de rocas entre Marte y Jú: "Millions of rocks between Mars and Jupiter."
lit.\u0027Misiones Venera (URSS): Venera 7 (: "Venera missions (USSR): Venera 7 (1970) was the first probe to transmit from the surface of another planet. Magellan (NASA) mapped the planet with radar in 1990–94 and Akatsuki (JAXA) studied its atmosphere."
lit.\u0027Muy caliente, con atmósfera densa: "Very hot, with a dense CO₂ atmosphere and retrograde rotation."
lit.\u0027Muy tenue, de oxígeno. Podría habe: "Very thin, of oxygen. There could be water vapor plumes."
lit.\u0027Muy tenue: ≈ 95 % CO₂, ≈ 2,8 % N₂: "Very thin: ≈ 95 % CO₂, ≈ 2.8 % N₂ and ≈ 1.9 % argon, with a pressure of ≈ 0.6 % of Earth's."
lit.\u0027New Horizons (NASA) lo sobrevoló e: "New Horizons (NASA) flew by it on July 14, 2015 and revealed mountains of water ice and nitrogen glaciers."
lit.\u0027New Horizons sobrevoló Arrokoth en: "New Horizons flew by Arrokoth in 2019, a two-lobed object that formed by the gentle merging of two bodies."
lit.\u0027no ha despejado su órbita de otros: "it has not cleared its orbit of other bodies"
lit.\u0027Observada de cerca por Galileo y J: "Observed up close by Galileo and Juno."
lit.\u0027Observado por SOHO, SDO, Solar Orb: "Observed by SOHO, SDO, Solar Orbiter and the Parker probe, which has come within about 6 million km of its surface."
lit.\u0027Orbita al revés: probablemente fue: "It orbits backward: it was probably captured."
lit.\u0027Orbita fuera del intenso cinturón: "It orbits outside Jupiter's intense radiation belt, so it has been proposed as a base for future exploration."
lit.\u0027Pioneer 11, Voyager 1 y 2 y Cassin: "Pioneer 11, Voyager 1 and 2 and Cassini–Huygens (2004–2017), which studied the system and released the Huygens probe onto Titan in 2005. Dragonfly (NASA) will fly to Titan in the 2030s."
lit.\u0027Pioneer, Voyager, Galileo (1995–20: "Pioneer, Voyager, Galileo (1995–2003), Juno (arrived in 2016) and Europa Clipper (launched in 2024, arriving in 2030)."
lit.\u0027Planeta enano con órbita muy excén: "Dwarf planet with a very eccentric and inclined orbit."
lit.\u0027Planeta enano desde 2006, cuando l: "A dwarf planet since 2006, when the IAU defined “planet” as a body that orbits the Sun, is nearly spherical and has cleared its orbit; Pluto does not meet the last condition. It is one of the largest objects in the Kuiper belt."
lit.\u0027Planetas rocosos: Mercurio, Venus,: "Rocky planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars"
lit.\u0027Plutón dejó de ser planeta en 2006: "Pluto stopped being a planet in 2006 because…"
lit.\u0027Plutón y Caronte giran en torno a: "Pluto and Charon revolve around a point located outside Pluto: they form almost a double planet. Between 1979 and 1999 it was closer to the Sun than Neptune."
lit.\u0027Por su lenta rotación y su órbita: "Because of its slow rotation and eccentric orbit, from some points on its surface the Sun rises, stops, goes backward and moves forward again. Even so, there is water ice in polar craters that are always in shadow."
lit.\u0027Programa Apolo (1969–1972: 12 astr: "Apollo program (1969–1972: 12 astronauts walked on it) and robotic missions such as Chang’e, Chandrayaan-3 and LRO. NASA's Artemis program seeks the return of astronauts."
lit.\u0027Región helada más allá de Neptuno: "Icy region beyond Neptune with millions of objects, the source of part of the short-period comets. It is home to Pluto and other dwarf planets (Eris, Haumea and Makemake)."
lit.\u0027Roca basáltica (los «mares») y ano: "Basaltic rock (the “seas”) and anorthosite (highlands), covered with regolith. There is water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters."
lit.\u0027Se acerca lentamente a Neptuno: en: "It is slowly approaching Neptune: in the distant future it could break apart and form rings."
lit.\u0027Se aleja de la Tierra unos 3,8 cm: "It moves away from Earth about 3.8 cm per year, and its attraction produces the tides."
lit.\u0027Según la tercera ley de Kepler, un: "According to Kepler's third law, a planet at 4 AU from the Sun would have a year of…"
lit.\u0027Solo la Voyager 2 lo ha visitado (: "Only Voyager 2 has visited it (1986). An orbital mission is the priority of planetary science for the next decade."
lit.\u0027Solo la Voyager 2 lo visitó (1989): "Only Voyager 2 visited it (1989) and discovered the Great Dark Spot, a storm that later disappeared."
lit.\u0027Su atmósfera de CO₂ produce un int: "Its CO₂ atmosphere produces an intense greenhouse effect"
lit.\u0027Su atmósfera densa de CO₂ atrapa e: "Its dense CO₂ atmosphere traps heat: ≈ 465 °C at the surface."
lit.\u0027Sus bandas claras y oscuras muestr: "Its light and dark bands show ancient tectonic activity."
lit.\u0027Tiene la atmósfera más fría del Si: "It has the coldest atmosphere in the Solar System (down to −224 °C), even though Neptune is much farther from the Sun."
lit.\u0027Tiene la superficie más craterizad: "It has the most heavily cratered surface in the Solar System and one of the oldest (≈ 4 billion years), a sign of little geological activity. It possibly harbors a subsurface ocean."
lit.\u0027Tiene volcanes activos en todo el: "It has active volcanoes all over the planet"
lit.\u0027Una persona de 60 kg, ¿en cuál de: "A 60 kg person, on which of these bodies would they weigh the most?"
lit.\u0027Una unidad astronómica (UA) equiva: "An astronomical unit (AU) is approximately equal to…"
lit.\u0027Único satélite natural de la Tierr: "Earth's only natural satellite and the fifth largest in the Solar System. It probably formed after the impact of a Mars-sized body with the early Earth. It always shows the same face because its rotation is locked to its orbit."
lit.\u0027Urano rueda de lado, probablemente: "Uranus rolls on its side, probably because of an ancient collision."
lit.\u0027Venus rota en 243 días terrestres: "Venus rotates in 243 Earth days and orbits the Sun in 225. Mercury rotates in 58.6 days and orbits in 88: its day is shorter than its year."
